diagram_math_checks.check: The tuple is strictly ordered in this example only; no ordering assumption is added to the general definition, which allows arbitrary points in R^d.

diagram_math_checks.justification: From Definition line 45, index 1 wins weak comparisons with indices 2 and 3. (x+2)^2<=x^2 iff x<=-1; (x+2)^2<=(x-2)^2 iff x<=0. Their intersection is x<=-1. The filled endpoint at -1 and left arrow encode this.
Strict comparison with index 1 gives x^2<(x+2)^2 iff x>-1; weak comparison with index 3 gives x^2<=(x-2)^2 iff x<=1. Open left/filled right endpoints encode exactly this.
Strict comparisons with indices 1 and 2 give x>0 and x>1, respectively. Their intersection is x>1, represented by an open endpoint and right arrow.

At -1 the distances to c_1,c_2 are both 1 and c_3 is farther; at 1 the distances to c_2,c_3 are both 1 and c_1 is farther. The smaller-index rule therefore assigns -1 to C_1 and 1 to C_2. For a Borel subset X the original definition explicitly intersects each full-domain cell with X. The illustration does not assert this partition for arbitrary measurable Q or compander boundaries.
